newsitem.title: UK: Iraq's Basrah Light crude offered in Europe -trade.
newsitem.headline: Iraq's Basrah Light crude offered in Europe -trade.

text.p: European refiners are being offered Iraqi Basrah Light crude barrels that contract lifters have failed to find homes for in the United States and the Far East, traders said.
But Basrah Light, which loads at the Gulf terminal of Mina al-Bakr, has found the same cool reception in Europe as elsewhere, they said.
"We have been offered (Basrah Light). But it's not workable to take to Europe," said one European refiner, who said he was offered the crude by a Russian trading house.
European demand for Iraqi crude has been more than satisfied by supplies of Kirkuk, which loads at the Mediterranean port of Ceyhan.
A Kirkuk cargo loading around March 10 was heard still unsold on Wednesday having been on offer for several days.

Traders said that buyers would be looking for a discount of at least 20 cents to the official selling price (OSP) for sales to Europe in March of Dated Brent -$1.55 a barrel. The OSP will drop to dated Brent -$1.65 in April.
Basrah Light only has official pricing structures for sales to the United States and the Far East.
But U.S. refiners have shunned recent offers of the Iraqi grade as weak demand and increasing availabilities of other sour crudes have pushed prices lower.
And a relatively short nomination period for loadings have made sales into the Far East tricky, traders said.
In an effort to spur sales, the price formula for sales of Basrah Light into the United States was revised down to a $3.90 discount to West Texas Intermediate crude from March 10.
This price will fall a further 15 cents in April in line with Saudi Arabian Arab Light prices to which the formula is tied.
